title: Preprocessor phase, macro hazards and include dependency management
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.

understand.concept: The preprocessor handles directives and macro expansion before later translation phases. Macros are token substitutions, so operator precedence, repeated argument evaluation, name collisions and include cycles can create subtle defects. Header guards or equivalent mechanisms control repeated inclusion.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding preprocessing helps diagnose expanded source, reduce hidden dependencies and design stable public headers.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: Parentheses protect grouping, but the macro may evaluate an argument more than once. Passing expressions with side effects is therefore unsafe.

practise.guidedTask: Expand the macro for MAX_VALUE(x++, y) and explain why it is dangerous.
practise.independentTask: Design a header with include guards and replace a risky function-like macro with a typed function where appropriate.
hints: Avoid side effects in macro arguments.
Use unique macro names and consistent include guards.
Inspect preprocessed output when macro expansion is confusing.
